### Generation 1
Your analysis then: Constant f scores 2/3. A two-step f with heights (1,2) already gives L=[0,1,4,4,0] and R=86/108≈0.7963, so the constant is far from optimal. This suggests monotone staircase shapes are the strong line. I will bet on (i) optimizing a two-block shape over cut/ratio, (ii) fine coordinate-wise refinement of the (1,2) pattern, and (iii) a genuinely different three-level staircase random search. All should use the full 30 s, returning the best seen.

### Generation 2
Your analysis then: Evidence: p0004's annealed 400-step smooth bump (0.8327) beats all structured searches; its convolution peak is near the centre (0.509) and has 38% of knots within 5% of max, so the goal is a broad flat top of f*f. p0007 shows multi-level structure helps (0.8248) but three coarse levels are not enough. I bet on three lines: (i) finer resolution made affordable by FFT convolution, (ii) many-block piecewise-constant optimization with sharp edges as a competing representation, (iii) carving a central notch / two bumps so f*f's central peak is lowered relative to its shoulders, flattening the top.

### Generation 3
Your analysis then: p0013 (0.8351) is the strongest, with an asymmetric broad convolution top peaking at 0.818 of support; 39% of knots are within 5% of max. Its annealer is stochastic and likely inefficient near the optimum. p0011's central notch failed, so symmetric carving is not the answer; p0012's block branch underperformed but was coarse (K=10). I bet on (i) exact analytic-gradient refinement of p0013, (ii) a smooth p-norm surrogate that directly penalizes the convolution peak, and (iii) revisiting the block branch with many more blocks seeded from p0013.

### Generation 4
Your analysis then: p0018's jump to 0.8788 came from exact gradient refinement; its f*f is already very flat (45% of knots within 0.1% of max) and asymmetric, peaking at 0.935 of support. The remaining weaknesses are likely the non-smooth single-knot max and a possible fine-scale local optimum. I bet on (i) an active-set subgradient over the near-max plateau, (ii) coarse-to-fine multi-resolution optimization to escape fine-scale traps, and (iii) high-p norm continuation to smooth the max, revisiting p0015 with a much better start and much larger p.
